I've implemented the solution, but my attempt to build and run the tests was denied by the permission system, so I couldn't verify it here.

## What I implemented

**`robot_name.h`** — a `robot` class in namespace `robot_name` with:
- `robot()` constructor — assigns a random name on construction
- `const std::string& name() const` — returns the current name (const, since the tests call it on `const robot`)
- `void reset()` — wipes the name and assigns a new one
- a static `std::unordered_set<std::string> _used_names` tracking every name ever handed out

**`robot_name.cpp`** — name generation:
- A process-wide `std::mt19937` engine seeded from `std::random_device`, so names don't follow a predictable sequence
- Names are built as 2 letters from `A–Z` plus 3 digits from `0–9` using uniform distributions (e.g. `RX837`)
- `generate_unique_name()` loops until it produces a name not already in `_used_names`, then records it — guaranteeing every robot (including one after `reset()`) gets a name no other robot has

This satisfies all five test cases: valid format, stable name across calls, distinct robots, reset producing a different name, and 1000 resets never colliding with previously seen names.

To verify, you can run:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DEXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build
./build/robot-name
```

If you'd like me to run the build myself, allow the shell permission and I'll do it.
